title: Idempotent SQS consumers (at-least-once delivery)
hook: SQS guarantees at-least-once delivery — your handler will see duplicates from retries, visibility timeouts, and producer resends. Idempotency is an application responsibility, not a queue feature.

blocks.text: An idempotent consumer produces the same side effect whether it processes a message once or five times. Common pattern: store an idempotency key (paymentId, messageId) in DynamoDB with conditional write before performing irreversible work. FIFO deduplication helps on the send side only — receive-side retries still require consumer idempotency.

entries.plainDefinition: Every message delivered one or more times; never lost after ack semantics.
entries.example: Visibility timeout retry delivers same message twice.

entries.plainDefinition: Unique token identifying one logical operation.
entries.example: paymentId ord-8821-charge used in DynamoDB conditional put.

entries.plainDefinition: Write succeeds only if attribute does not exist — atomic claim.
Business outcome happens once even if message runs N times.
entries.example: Customer charged once despite duplicate delivery.

blocks.text: Double-charge lawsuits start with 'SQS is exactly-once, right?' Payment, inventory reservation, and email send all need idempotent handlers. Senior interviews ask for DynamoDB claim pattern, TTL on idempotency records, and what happens when claim succeeds but downstream fails.

blocks.title: Interview framing
blocks.body: Say: at-least-once from SQS; exactly-once effect from idempotency store. Claim before side effect; store result for replay.

sections.heading: How it works step by step

items.title: Extract key
items.body: Use business id (orderId) not SQS messageId alone — messageId changes on redrive.

items.title: Conditional claim
items.body: PutItem with attribute_not_exists — winner proceeds, loser returns cached result.

items.title: Perform work
items.body: Charge card, send email — only after successful claim.

items.title: Record outcome
items.body: Update item with status COMPLETED and result for duplicate queries.

diagram.title: Idempotency claim pattern
diagram.source:
flowchart TD
  M[SQS message] --> H[Handler]
  H --> C{Conditional put\nidempotency key}
  C -->|exists| R[Return stored result]
  C -->|new| W[Perform side effect]
  W --> U[Update status COMPLETED]
  U --> D[Delete SQS message]

snippet.explanation: Stripe idempotencyKey aligns with DynamoDB claim — defense in depth.

snippet.label: CloudFormation — idempotency table with TTL
snippet.code:
Resources:
  IdempotencyTable:
    Type: AWS::DynamoDB::Table
    Properties:
      TableName: idempotency-keys
      BillingMode: PAY_PER_REQUEST
      AttributeDefinitions:
        - AttributeName: pk
          AttributeType: S
      KeySchema:
        - AttributeName: pk
          KeyType: HASH
      TimeToLiveSpecification:
        AttributeName: ttl
        Enabled: true
snippet.explanation: TTL expires old keys after 24–72 hours — balance storage vs replay window.

snippet.label: CLI — detect duplicate processing in logs
snippet.code:
aws logs start-query \
  --log-group-name /aws/lambda/payment-processor \
  --start-time $(date -u -v-1H +%s) \
  --end-time $(date -u +%s) \
  --query-string 'fields orderId | filter @message like /duplicate skip/ | stats count() by orderId | filter count > 1'
snippet.explanation: Instrument skip path in logs to measure duplicate rate — proves idempotency is firing.

blocks.title: Pitfalls to avoid
blocks.body: Using SQS messageId as idempotency key — changes on redrive. Claim after charge instead of before. No TTL — table grows forever. IN_PROGRESS stuck forever when worker crashes mid-flight — add lease expiry.

blocks.text: How to prove it in production: metric duplicate_skip_count / messages_processed. Load test with visibility timeout shorter than handler — zero double charges if idempotency works. For IN_PROGRESS lease: conditional update with expiresAt; second worker can reclaim after expiry.

blocks.title: What gets you rejected in interviews
blocks.body: Saying 'FIFO gives exactly-once end to end.' Strong answer: FIFO deduplicates sends; consumers still need idempotency for visibility retries and partial batch failures.

interviewTakeaways: SQS is at-least-once — idempotency is mandatory for side effects.
Conditional DynamoDB put before irreversible work; store COMPLETED result for duplicates.
Use business key (orderId) not messageId; TTL old keys; handle IN_PROGRESS lease.
60s: Claim in DynamoDB before charge. FIFO dedup is send-only. At-least-once means duplicates.
Follow-up: what if claim succeeds but charge fails?
commonPitfalls: Trusting FIFO alone for payment idempotency — rejection answer.
Strong answer: consumer conditional write regardless of queue type.
messageId as key — wrong on DLQ redrive.
No handling of stuck IN_PROGRESS after worker crash.
